spatial_claims.claim: G is constructed as a leg of a right triangle with hypotenuse A and other leg B, so that A^2 = B^2 + G^2 (by 1.47)

configuration_map: The proof operates almost entirely in the domain of ratios and commensurability. The only geometric object constructed is line G (Step 8), defined via the Pythagorean theorem as the leg of a right triangle. After construction, G participates only in algebraic ratio chains (Steps 9-11). No spatial relationships between points, no ray orderings, no angle decompositions, and no inside/outside claims are made.
skip_reason: The proof is fundamentally algebraic/proportional, dealing with number-theoretic ratio properties and commensurability definitions. The single geometric construction (right triangle in Step 8) is entirely standard and incidental. All reasoning proceeds through ratio manipulation (separando, ex aequali) and commensurability criteria (10.6, 10.9). No meaningful spatial configuration claims exist to check for mutual consistency. This is typical of Book 10 propositions on commensurable/incommensurable magnitudes.
